_comment: The wheels VSCodroid mirrors, so that pip install of a package with a compiled
part can succeed on a device that has no compiler and cannot run one.
Every entry is a prebuilt Android wheel built by the Termux User Repository,
not by us. `url` records where it came from so the provenance chain is
auditable; `sha256` is what pip enforces once the wheel is mirrored into our
own release.
psutil is the exception, because nobody publishes an Android wheel of it. Its
`url` is Termux's own python-psutil package, built for the same interpreter.
build-wheelhouse.py checks that .deb against Termux's signed index before
pinning `source-sha256`, and repacks its files into a wheel without changing
them. ipykernel requires psutil, so without it the Jupyter extension cannot
install a kernel. Termux's pool keeps only a package's current revision, so
when Termux rebuilds python-psutil the entry has to be re-pinned; the wheel
already on the release stays where it is.
Changing a version is a reviewed diff to this file, deliberately:
there is no scheduled job that moves them, because for these names PyPI has no
compatible wheel at any version, so whatever is pinned here is what users get
until someone edits it.
python-version must match the interpreter the APK carries. That version is
auto-detected from the Termux index by scripts/download-python.sh and can move
without anyone deciding, which would invalidate every wheel here at once;
scripts/check-wheelhouse-abi.py is the gate that makes that a build failure
rather than a user's pip install finding no candidate weeks later.
Held back deliberately: scipy and scikit-learn. scipy's wheel carries
libandroid-complex-math with LOAD segments aligned to 0x1000 where Android 16
needs 0x4000, so scipy.special would fail to import on 16 KB-page devices and
work everywhere else. scripts/build-wheelhouse.py refuses it, and will keep
refusing it until upstream rebuilds, which is how it gets back in.
Also held back: lxml. Its wheel links GNU libiconv (LGPL-2.1), libxml2 and
libxslt statically and carries only lxml's own notices, so re-hosting it would
redistribute an LGPL library with neither its licence nor an offer of source.
pandas compiles in UltraJSON, klib and other vendored code whose licences ask
for their notices, and its wheel carries only pandas' own. Unlike lxml's, those
notices are all in pandas' source distribution, so `notices` names it and the
paths to take, and build-wheelhouse.py publishes them beside the wheel.
The page for this manifest is docs/site/wheels/<python-version>/wheels.html.
When python-version moves, the previous version's page stays: devices still on
the older APK read it.
